_comment: KNOWN-BAD / REJECTED regression example. This is a real API proposal (from data/confirmed_stitch_patterns.json's 'filet mesh' entry, produced by engine/vision.py's get_stitch_recipe() during real testing on 2026-09-05), preserved here so it is not lost or silently reproposed as new. It is NOT the canonical v2 reference example -- see contracts/examples/stitch_recipe_v2_structural_example.json for a different, non-rejected recipe candidate for the SAME broad stitch-family label (filet mesh). Its status is REJECTED, not AI_PROPOSED: its row-1 repeat conflicts with the specific target construction being tested (the halter/corset top's open filet-mesh grid) -- it lacks the per-repeat skipped foundation chain that construction needs to create its open grid, so it cannot produce the intended structure. That structural mismatch is sufficient basis to reject it without needing a fresh physical swatch. This is not a claim that comparing golden-fixture arithmetic alone proves crochet truth -- see known_issues and verification.reason below for the actual basis.
name: Filet Mesh (rejected AI candidate)

foundation_formula.note: foundation_count = repeat_multiple * requested_repeat_count + additional_chains. additional_chains=3 covers 2 fresh chain links (setup's CH 2) plus 1 skipped foundation chain (setup's SKIP 1).

known_issues: Row-1 repeat lacks a per-repeat skipped foundation chain -- every repeat iteration consumes only the DC (1 stitch), so the row-1 repeat never opens a gap in the foundation. The specific target construction this candidate was meant to describe (the halter/corset top's open filet-mesh grid, as worked in this project's regression fixtures at tests/golden/halter_mesh_row1_*.json) needs a per-repeat SKIP to create that open grid; this candidate omits it entirely and therefore does not create the intended open foundation grid.

Mathematical consistency does not establish filet-mesh correctness -- this candidate's foundation/row arithmetic computes cleanly (no internal contradiction), but internal consistency alone cannot show it creates the target construction's open grid. Only comparing what each repeat iteration actually does (open a gap, or not) surfaces the missing SKIP -- a structural/definitional comparison, not proof derived from fixture arithmetic passing. Passing or comparing golden-fixture arithmetic alone does not, by itself, prove crochet correctness in either direction.

Chain-2 (row 1 setup) vs. chain-3 (later-row turning chain) lead-in length mismatch for the same DC-based repeat, flagged 2026-09-05 in data/concierge_log.csv and never resolved -- a further, independent reason to distrust this candidate even before the missing-SKIP issue is considered.

verification.reason: Row-1 repeat conflicts with the specific target construction being tested (the halter/corset top's open filet-mesh grid): it lacks the per-repeat skipped foundation chain that construction requires to create its open grid, so it does not produce the intended structure. This is a structural/definitional mismatch with the target construction, not a claim that passing or comparing golden-fixture arithmetic alone proves crochet truth -- those fixtures document real hand-crocheted observations and expected engine behavior, including their own unresolved 4-vs-5 DC discrepancy, and are not treated as infallible ground truth here. No fresh physical swatch of this specific candidate was required to reach this rejection.
